sentences.text: The petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of one Md.Ashraf Mansoori in RTA.

2. The averments of the petition in brief are as follows; That on 05.08.2021 at about 10.55 A.M.,
while one Ashraf Mansoori was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA- 51-Y-0206 from Nagawara towards Hegde Nagar in Thanisandra main road, a BMTC bus bearing No.KA-01-FA- 2322 came from same direction in a negligent manner, dashed to the said Ashraf Mansoori who fell down and died on the spot.
That the petitioners are the minor daughter and parents of the deceased.
That the deceased was working as tailor and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
That the petitioners have spent more than Rs.80,000/- towards final rituals.
Thus prays to grant compensation as sought for.
3. Per contra, the respondent in the written statement denies that there is negligence on the part of the deceased and prays to dismiss the petition.
4. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, the following issues were framed my learned predecessor.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 05.08.2021 at about 10.55 A.M., when the deceased Md.Ashraf mansoori was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA- 51-Y-0206, in front of Kanthi sweet,
Thanisandra main road, Sarayipalya, Bengaluru, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-FA-2322 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased,
caused the accident and as a result, the deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot as alleged by them?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove their case, the petitioner no.2 got examined herself as P.W.1 and has produced 14 documents on her behalf.
The respondent got examined the driver of the BMTC bus as RW-1.

6. Heard the arguments from the counsel for the petitioner and the counsel for respondent and perused the materials placed before me.
7.

My findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : in the Affirmative, Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:

sentences.text: 8. Issue No.1:
In order to substantiate the allegation, the petitioner No.2 got examined herself as PW-1 and furnished totally documents.
The driver of the respondent bus got examined as DW-1.

To further prove the case, the PW-1 has filed her affidavit in lieu of examination in chief and got produced the copy of the FIS as Ex.P.2, which is lodged by one Asgar Ali, the brother of said deceased Ashraf, where he submits that he got information about the accident on 05.08.2021 at about 11.00 AM., while he was in work and found his brother dead with Chest injuries in the hospital.

The FIR is as per Ex.P.1 in Cr.No.57/21 alleging offences punishable under section 279, and 304(A) of IPC.
9.

The spot panchanama and sketch are at Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.5 depicting the manner of accident and shows that the accident took place while BMTC bus moved towards the left side of the road, which was one way.
The MVA report shows scratching of left side body of BMTC bus, where as front right side portion of the vehicle of said Ashraf/deceased is reported to be damaged.
This clearly goes to show that the BMTC bus tried to move to the left side, causing collusion with the vehicle of the deceased to its right portion.
Inquest report and PM report are at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 where opinion as to cause of death is given as due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained.

Final report is against the driver of the BMTC, as per Ex.P.7, alleging offences punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
10.
The respondent is not denying the involvement of the bus in the accident.
But denies the negligence on their part in the accident.
PW-1 is not an eye witness to the accident and submits that she got information from the police station regarding accident and she is ignorant of the manner of the accident.

Thus the driver of the BMTC who drove the vehicle/bus at the time of accident was examined as RW-1, who has deposed that on 05.08.2021, while he was proceeding on schedule trip from K.R.Market to Yelahanka, near Sarayipalya bus stop, opposite to Kanthi sweets, the deceased without head gear was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
That as the road was under repair, the deceased tried to over take the slow moving bus from left side as there was no space and thus there was collusion in between the vehicles.
Regarding the same when questioned by the counsel for the petitioner, RW-1 submits that the final report is not challenged and that the vehicle was released by them.
No eye witness are examined.

Thus when the involvement of the vehicle is not disputed, the sketch showing the turning of the heavy bus towards left side in one way road, coupling with charge sheet, this court can come to theconclusion that the accident occurred due to negligence on part of the driver of the BMTC bus.
Thus above point is answered in affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
The petitioner No.1 is alleged to be daughter of the deceased and being minor is represented by her grand mother the petitioner No.2.
The counsel for the respondent disputes the relationship of the deceased with petitioner No.1.
Thus PW-1 submits that the deceased had divorced his wife.
But the daughter (Petitioner No.1) remained with them.

To show the divorce in between the deceased and his wife, the " Khulanama Agreement" was marked as Ex.P.13, which was on 12.12.2015, executed in between Heena Kausar and Mohammed Ashraf Ali, where they have submitted that they got married in 2013 and has one female child Falak Naaz, born on 03.06.2014,
and 1 st party wife has retained the custody of the child.

Thus it is clear that the deceased was Falak Naaz vs The Manager on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75413524/
3 divorced and the petitioner No.1 is his child.

sentences.text: 12. The counsel for the respondent submits that the petitioner No.1 is in the custody of the wife of the deceased and not dependent as per Ex.P.13.
Though the wife is divorced the child has nothing to do with the same.
The right of a child, its dependency on both mother and father cannot be taken away though they live separately from each other.

Therefore the petitioner No.1, when proved that she is the daughter of the deceased, and being minor is considered to be completely dependent on her father, whether she resides with her mother or grand mother.
Therefore the contention of the respondent does not hold any water, and thus petitioner No.1 has lost love and affection of her father.
13. The petitioners have produced copy of adhaar card as Ex.P.10 pertaining to the deceased, which is not disputed, showing his date of birth as 26.11.1987.

Thus the deceased was aged about 35 years and appropriate multiplier for the said age is 16.
14.
The petitioners submits that the deceased was working as tailor Designer (cutting master) and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But have not produced any document to show the same.
Accordingly the notional income to an extent of Rs.14,250/- can be considered.

15. Since the petitioner No.1 is the daughter and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased, there were 3 dependents on the income of the deceased and 1/3rd of the salary must be deducted towards personal expenses and 40% of income should be added as future prospects.

Therefore the petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and petitioner No.2 and 3 to an extent of Rs.40,000/- each and consortium and petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled to Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate.
Thus Loss of dependency calculation is as follows:
Yearly income of the deceased 14250X12= 1,71,000/-
1. Calculating 40% future prospects:
40% X 1,71,000 = 68,400/- Adding 40% future prospects: 1,71,000+68,400=
2,39,400/-
2.

calculation of 1/3rd income of Rs.2,39,400/-
2,39,400 X 1/3 = 79,800/-

3. Deducting 1/3 personal expenses:
Rs.2,39,400-79,800/- 1,59,600/-
4. Calculating loss of dependency 1,59,600 X '16' 25,53,600/-

4 16.
Towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies Rs. 15,000/-

4. Loss of consortium Rs. 80,000/-
(Petitioner No.2 & 3 )
5. Loss of love and affection Rs. 40,000/-
 (Petitioner No.1 )
 Total Rs. 27,03,600/-
17.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,03,600/- which can be rounded to Rs.27,04,000/-.

18. Liability:-
In this case, there is no disputed fact that the respondent is the insurer and also the owner of the said BMTC bus bearing No.KA-01-FA-2322, which caused the accident.
The respondent has failed to prove that the insurance company is not liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.

Hence, this issue is answered accordingly burdening the respondent to pay the compensation to the petitioners, along with the present Bank rate of interest at 6%.
19. Issue No.3:
After having answered issue No.1 and 2 as supra, I hold that, the petition filed by the petitioner is fit to be allowed in Part.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,04,000/- with interest @ 6% pa.,
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within two months from the date of judgment.
After deposit, the petitioners are entitled to share in the ratio of 4:3:3, with cost and interest and consortium as under.

The petitioner No.2 to 3 are entitled for a sum of Rs.8,11,200/-each.

After deposit, 60% share of the petitioners shall be released and deposit 40% share of compensation amount as FD in their name with any nationalized or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of three years.
